args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it was promoted to production when the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. A follow-up check shows the service is healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the current state. It also lists two follow-ups: finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and finding out why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
